task.description: WF-02 Step 2a (ELIXIR-DEV) for run-id WF02-REQ019-20260816: implement lib/letflow/design/req019-tenant-realm-binding.md (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS) exactly — Letflow.Identity.Tenant.create_changeset/3 and update_changeset/2, Letflow.Identity.resolve_tenant_by_realm/1, resolve_realm_by_tenant/1, verify_realm_ownership/2.
acceptance_criteria: resolveTenantByRealm(idp_realm_id) and resolveRealmByTenant(tenant_id) both work against REQ-015's tenants table, tested with the seeded default tenant (bpm-default)
attempting to bind a second tenant to an already-bound idp_realm_id is rejected (unique index or explicit changeset validation), not silently overwritten

attempting to change an existing tenant's idp_realm_id via the normal update changeset is rejected or the changeset simply omits idp_realm_id from its allowed fields — whichever approach is taken, it's stated explicitly in the moduledoc
a realm-ownership guard function exists that rejects a (tenant_id, external_realm) pair where external_realm is not the realm bound to tenant_id

result.summary: Implemented lib/letflow/design/req019-tenant-realm-binding.md exactly as specified, no deviations. lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex gained create_changeset/3 (tenant, attrs, oidc_mode :: :enabled | :disabled) and update_changeset/2, plus a private validate_default_tenant_pinning/1 and validate_idp_realm_id_required/2 helper pair implementing the design's §3.2 conditional-required and default-tenant-pinning rules. create_changeset/3's cast/3 list is [:slug, :display_name, :status, :idp_realm_id]; update_changeset/2's is [:display_name, :status] only -- idp_realm_id and slug are both structurally absent, confirmed by direct grep of the diff. unique_constraint(:idp_realm_id, name: :tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index) names REQ-015's actual partial index character-for-character (confirmed against priv/repo/migrations/20260816000001_create_tenants.exs line 40). Moduledoc updated per design §10: states immutability is structural (cast/3 omission, not a runtime rejection check), states no admin rotation function is built and why, states create_changeset/3 takes an explicit oidc_mode argument rather than reading Application config. lib/letflow/identity.ex gained resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 (Repo.get_by(Tenant, idp_realm_id: ...) -> {:ok, tenant} | {:error, :not_found}), resolve_realm_by_tenant/1 (Repo.get(Tenant, tenant_id) -> {:ok, realm_or_nil} | {:error, :not_found}), and verify_realm_ownership/2, which re-queries via resolve_realm_by_tenant/1 internally (confirmed in diff -- does not accept a pre-resolved realm as a third argument, per design §6.2's trust-boundary decision) and returns :ok | {:error, :realm_tenant_mismatch} | {:error, :not_found} covering all four edge cases from design §6.1 (match, mismatch, tenant-not-found, nil-realm-tenant) in three case clauses (the nil and mismatched-non-nil cases share one clause, {:ok, _mismatched_or_nil} -> {:error, :realm_tenant_mismatch}, which is behaviorally identical to the design's four-case enumeration -- empirically confirmed both sub-cases produce the correct output, see below). @moduledoc gained a citation of realm_tenant_binding.zig and adp-04a/04b appended after the existing REQ-018 citations, not replacing them. provisioning_error() type left unmodified (confirmed by grep -- only two references, both pre-existing, both scoped to provision_oidc_user/3's own @spec). No new file created. No new migration -- confirmed empirically (see verification below), matching the design's §1 explicit statement. Zero design deviations found; the design's own empirically-flagged open questions (OQ-1 through OQ-6) are genuinely open/deferred as the design states, none blocked correct implementation.
result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) -- this is explicitly a tenant-data/cross-tenant-boundary path per the routing instructions.
